chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who forgot to perform the second prostration until he stood up and remembered while standing that he had not prostrated, he said: 'Let him prostrate as long as he has not bowed. And if he raised himself up and remembered after his bowing that he had not prostrated, let him continue with his prayer until he gives the salutation, then he prostrates it, for it is a missed obligation.'

And he said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If he doubts the bowing after he has prostrated, let him continue; and if he doubts the prostration after he has stood up, let him continue. Whatever he doubts of what he has already passed and entered into another, let him continue upon it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person forgets a prostration and remembers it after standing up in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'continuity in prayer' (istishab al-hal) by distinguishing between forgetting a pillar before fully transitioning versus after, thereby determining whether the missed act is immediate or treated as a subsequent obligation (qada). It further clarifies the rule of doubt (shakk) in pillars, instructing the worshipper to proceed if the doubt arises after moving beyond the specific action, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for certainty over lingering doubt. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, ensuring the validity of prayer despite minor human error without requiring full repetition.
